recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If the resolved code definition needs future changes, handle them through HL7 Terminology/UTG or THO maintenance rather than by editing the current core FHIR source checkout.
issue_request: FHIR-15525 was Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification. It asked whether AllergyIntolerance verificationStatus=unconfirmed with clinicalStatus=resolved should be disallowed or clarified; Patient Care decided no invariant was needed and approved clarifying the resolved code definition to say re-exposure could be accidental, unplanned, or outside a clinical setting.
initial_application: Commit 722ed5c93f applied GF#15525 by adding the requested re-exposure sentence to the AllergyIntolerance clinicalStatus/resolved definition in source/allergyintolerance/allergyintolerance-spreadsheet.xml. Later FHIR-17743 converted clinicalStatus and verificationStatus to CodeableConcept and introduced terminology files, and FHIR-19634 refined the AllergyIntolerance clinical-status definitions while preserving the FHIR-15525 clarification.
additional_context: AllergyIntolerance remains an active resource in source/fhir.ini, and the current StructureDefinition binds AllergyIntolerance.clinicalStatus to ValueSet/allergyintolerance-clinical. The current core ValueSet includes http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/allergyintolerance-clinical, while commit 5c0494aacf removed UTG terminology content from the core build. The published THO CodeSystem currently has the resolved definition with the FHIR-15525 re-exposure sentence. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting FHIR-15525 evidence; a later refuted-status discussion led to FHIR-28458 and does not reverse this issue.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. No core source change was made because duplicating the external THO code definition in core would be redundant and risk terminology drift.
